title: Acceptance-test citation check: unscoped to the thread, and silently exempt after close
body:
Two edges on adjacent lines of `contract_report/3` (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/contract.rs:683-690`). They are filed together deliberately: a reader who fixes the first without seeing the second will conclude the citation corpus is sound, and it is not.

## Edge 1 -- the citation check is unscoped to the thread, so another thread's row satisfies it

`contract.rs:689` is `!refs.carries_id(path, &t.id)`. The check takes a path and a LOCAL id, and AT ids are only locally unique -- `AT-02.1` exists in many threads at once. So a citation is accepted whenever the cited file contains the literal string anywhere, including on a line that names a different thread entirely.

**Reproduction, Lamplight 2026-09-05.** Minting two rows on ST0268 one command apart:

- `intent at new ST0268 AT-02.2 --file apps/lamplight/test/lamplight/media/entity_media_test.exs` was REFUSED: "does not carry the literal id AT-02.2". Correct behaviour.
- `intent at new ST0268 AT-02.1 --file apps/lamplight/test/lamplight/media/tiering_test.exs` was ACCEPTED. No row in that file declares ST0268 AT-02.1. What it carries is `describe "decide/5 -- the ST0261 WP-02 theme axis (ST0261 AT-02.1, ST0261 AT-02.2)"`.

The direction is the point: **the guard is strict enough to refuse the honest case and loose enough to pass the dishonest one.** With a locally-unique id namespace, collision is the default condition rather than bad luck -- `AT-02.2` alone occurs in eight files across six threads in this one estate. The false positive renders identically to a verified citation, so nothing downstream can tell them apart. It was caught only because the sibling refusal made the pair inconsistent; had both been accepted, the result would have been a green row and a manufactured coverage edge.

Estate scan (vc, independently): three green rows cite a file where the id appears ONLY on lines naming a different thread -- ST0290 AT-02.1, ST0327 AT-02.1, ST0347 AT-05.1.

Fix shape: scope the match to the thread, ie require the id to appear qualified by its thread id (the convention every well-formed row in this estate already follows, `ST0261 AT-02.1`), or pass the thread id into `carries_id` and match the pair.

## Edge 2 -- enforcement ends at close, and no output says so

Two lines up, the arm is guarded `!completed && !refs.carries_id(...)`. The exemption is DELIBERATE and documented at `contract.rs:667`: *"L3 is exempt on a closed thread: retrofitting id labels into a completed thread's tests is archaeology."* That reasoning is sound and this issue does not ask for it to be reverted -- a gate that re-litigated closed threads forever would be useless, and citations that were true when written go stale honestly as files are renamed and tests refactored.

**The defect is narrower: no output anywhere distinguishes "checked and true" from "was true at close, unchecked since".** Both render as a green row with a file path, so a closed thread's coverage reads as current evidence indefinitely.

Measured across the Lamplight estate (vc): of 287 green rows with a file on completed threads, 164 cite a file that no longer carries the id. On WIP threads the figure is 0 of 252, because there the gate is running.

**One correction to that framing, from reading the source rather than the numbers.** The `!completed` guard covers ONLY the carries-id arm. The file-EXISTENCE arm above it (`!refs.resolves(path)`) is unguarded and still runs on closed threads, so the 37 rows citing a file that no longer exists are still caught today. The invisible population is the 164, not 201.

Fix shape: no new enforcement -- just make the scope visible. A closed thread's rendered rows should say the citation is unverified-since-close rather than reading as checked.

## Why the two belong together

Each is a green whose real scope is narrower than the sentence it renders as, which is the same family as the coverage-inversion where an AT stayed satisfied while the criterion it covered had become false. A gate that cannot state its own population reads exactly like coverage.
